stories.title: PaperPilot – Zero-Cloud, Pure-Rust PDF Engine with WASM and MCP
stories.author: vardhan1237

topComments.author: vardhan1237
topComments.text: Hi HN, I built PaperPilot because I was frustrated by the privacy trade-offs of modern PDF utilities. Whenever you need to split, merge, compress, or sign a confidential document (tax forms, legal contracts, medical paperwork) using online tools, your files are transmitted to a third-party server. Most "free" tools retain copies or run in closed-source cloud environments. PaperPilot is a 100% zero-cloud, local-first engine written in pure Rust (built on top of lopdf, pdf-writer, and image). 0 bytes are ever sent to an external server. Key aspects of the project: 1. Penta-Interface Architecture: Instead of building just another web app or CLI, the same core Rust operations run across 5 surfaces: - Terminal CLI: High-throughput local processing and bash scripting. - Local Desktop App: Native cross-platform GUI built with Tauri 2 and Svelte 5. - Client-Side Web: Runs 100% inside your browser via WebAssembly ( https://usepaperpilot.com/ ). - REST / Gateway API: Standalone local daemon (localhost:7823) for local microservices. - Model Context Protocol (MCP): Connects local AI agents (Claude Desktop, Cursor, OpenCode) directly to local PDF tools so LLMs can inspect, redact, and sign PDFs on disk without cloud upload. 2. Capabilities (75+ Tools): - Standard operations: Merge, split, rotate, reorder, burst, booklet imposition, and N-up grid. - Privacy & Compliance: Local PII regex redaction (SSNs, cards, emails), metadata striping, and digital signature verification. - Document Extraction: PDF to structured Markdown tables (no coordinate loss), PDF to JSON, and pure-Rust layout analysis. - Offline RAG: Embedded vector store (libsql_vector) with an actionable visual citation canvas. 3. Performance & License: - Average operation latency is ~20ms to 130ms. - 100% Free and Open Source under the Apache 2.0 license. The GitHub repository is at https://github.com/KrushnaVardhanReddy/PaperPilot and the browser-based WASM sandbox is live at https://usepaperpilot.com/ . I’d love to hear your feedback on the architecture, performance benchmarks, and any edge-case PDF formats we should test against!

jobs.text: I’m Chris, VP Engineering at Fazeshift. We’re nine engineers plus our Founder/CTO and me, and I’m hiring someone who can help us do more, better: increase both what we can build and the quality and sophistication of the software we build. Accounts receivable sounds boring until you look under the hood. It sits at the intersection of money, business relationships, software systems of various vintages, and a huge amount of repetitive human work. Instead of giving finance teams another dashboard to stare at, we’re building AI agents that actually do the work across billing, collections, payments, cash application, and the systems connecting them. We’ve grown revenue 12x since 2024, and eight unicorns now run AR on Fazeshift. A big part of what makes the engineering interesting is that we’re intentionally not the system of record. Our customers already run on ERPs, CRMs, banks, billing systems, payment processors, spreadsheets, and internal software, so we have to understand state across systems we don’t control, act safely in them, and recover when reality disagrees with what an API says should have happened. A timeout doesn’t necessarily mean a write failed. Webhooks can arrive late or twice. A payment may not contain enough information to identify an invoice. In those cases, blindly retrying can be exactly the wrong thing to do. We use coding agents heavily ourselves. Engineers use Conductor, stacked PRs, Linear, and multiple frontier models every day, with internal skills and tooling that let agents drive and validate our local development environment. We’re especially interested in engineers whose development workflow has already materially changed because of coding agents: people who are comfortable delegating meaningful work, keeping independent threads moving in parallel, debugging where agents get stuck, and improving the surrounding system when the workflow breaks down. But generated code is still your code . Judgment, debugging, systems thinking, taste, and understanding what actually shipped matter more here, not less. Our development style is roughly: design enough to find the shape of the problem, then build to learn. There’s a short distance here between noticing a problem, deciding what should happen, building it, and seeing the result in production with our customers. You’ll own meaningful problems from ambiguity through design, implementation, rollout, and production, and you’ll work directly with the people affected by what you build. We’re looking for 5+ years of professional experience, strong TypeScript/full-stack skills, solid systems judgment, and real production ownership. No fintech background needed. infoqArticles.description: ReadyOn has detailed a four-layer tenant isolation architecture for its Harmony platform on Amazon EKS. The design combines Kubernetes namespaces, dedicated Karpenter node pools, VPC security groups, and per-tenant Aurora databases, with controls evaluated against a 10-stage multi-tenant threat model focused on cross-tenant access and lateral movement. By Leela Kumili
infoqArticles.author: Leela Kumili

infoqArticles.title: Article: The Evolution of Agentic Harnesses: From Chains to Graph to Code
infoqArticles.description: Agentic LLM systems have moved from linear prompt chains to graph-based workflows and, more recently, code-executing harnesses. Chains are simple but fragile, graphs add branching, retries, and validation, and code harnesses verify outputs through execution. The article advises validating model outputs and choosing the least complex design that meets reliability, speed, and cost needs. By Karthik
infoqArticles.author: Karthik Ramgopal

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare’s Auto Router Rates Each Request for Stakes, from the Most Recent Turns
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare has released Auto Router in public beta through AI Gateway, picking a model per request from a classifier that scores complexity, ambiguity, stakes and context dependence. Cloudflare’s own benchmark puts it ten points below Claude Opus 5.5 on success rate at a third of the cost, and practitioners have questioned how stakes survive a long agent session. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: MCP C# SDK 2.0 Makes HTTP Stateless by Default and Adds Multi Round-Trip Requests
infoqArticles.description: Microsoft announced version 2.0 of the official MCP C# SDK, which implements the 2026-07-28 revision of the Model Context Protocol with stateless HTTP servers by default, standardised routing headers and Multi Round-Trip Requests. Releases 2.1 to 2.3 have since added hybrid session serving, a subscriptions/listen handler and a series of discovery, OAuth and shutdown fixes. By Edin Kapić
infoqArticles.author: Edin Kapić

infoqArticles.title: PHP Patches Two Critical RCE Flaws That Were Already Under Attack
infoqArticles.description: PHP released 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36, and 8.2.35 to fix two critical vulnerabilities allowing unauthenticated remote code execution. Amazon recorded an exploitation attempt four days before the patches shipped, and operators spent the day working out whether they ran PHP, where to get the package, and how to tell it had landed. By Steef-Jan Wiggers
infoqArticles.author: Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
infoqArticles.description: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. infoqArticles.author: Andrew Hoblitzell

infoqArticles.title: Google ML Drift Accelerates On-Device AI Inference Across Diverse GPUs
infoqArticles.description: Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts the complexities of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: PingCAP Breach Exposes Customer Records and Source Code
infoqArticles.description: PingCAP recently confirmed unauthorized access to its internal systems and the theft of source code and customer-related data. The attacker, cyber extortion group FulcrumSec, claimed to have stolen 10.6 TB of data, including TiDB Cloud control-plane records, customer SQL statements, API keys, connection logs, billing information, internal documents, and 413 private source-code repositories. By Ren

infoqArticles.title: Google Optimizes Agent Development Kit's 200K-line Python Codebase Overnight with Gemini 4 Argon
infoqArticles.description: Google explained how an 11-hour unattended run of Gemini 4 Argon produced two accepted optimizations for Google Agent Development Kit's codebase, reducing in-memory session-preparation overhead by about 40% in long sessions and cold package import time by 21%. By Sergio De Simone
infoqArticles.author: Sergio De Simone

infoqArticles.title: Google’s Data Agent Kit Hits GA, Splitting Agent Guardrails Between Skills and IAM
infoqArticles.description: Google has made Data Agent Kit generally available, a free set of MCP tools and 37 open-source skills that connect coding agents to more than fifteen Google Data Cloud services. Two kinds of guardrail ship with it, and practitioners need to tell them apart: one is a skill asking the agent to stop, the other an IAM deny policy that refuses the call. By Steef-Jan Wiggers

infoqArticles.title: Cloudflare Reclaims 100 TB of RAM by Optimizing Consistent Hashing
infoqArticles.description: Cloudflare recently documented how it reduced the memory footprint of its internal load-balancing service by more than 100 TB by optimizing the Rust implementation of consistent hashing in pingora-ketama. The changes compacted hash-ring entries and used statistical analysis of hash distribution and collision rates to reduce the number of hashes per backend by about 90%. By Renato Losio

infoqArticles.title: CSIRO Uses Serverless Architecture to Query 100x More Genomic Variants on AWS

The system combines Amazon S3, Lambda, Athena and DynamoDB, using metadata indexes and HTTP byte range requests to query compressed genomic regions. Tests reported 1.52 second average latency for 10,000 base pair queries. By Leela Kumili
